. A snapshot is a table that dbt maintains for you, where every change in a source table becomes a new row with a validity period. Snapshots are an official exam objective (1.10, "creating snapshots in YAML"), and the exam likes them because they are full of small, precise rules: which strategy needs which config, what
contains, what happens to deleted rows, which command runs them. This chapter gives you all those rules, and you will see each one happen in your own project.
A snapshot is a table that dbt builds from a source and then updates on every

. Since dbt 1.9 you declare snapshots in YAML, and because history cannot be rebuilt from the source, you protect snapshot tables and run them often.

A dbt snapshot is SCD Type 2, built and maintained automatically.

Think of a whiteboard in a shop. Every morning the manager erases yesterday's prices and writes today's prices. If you only look at the whiteboard, you can never know last week's price of a croissant. A snapshot is a notebook next to the whiteboard. Each time you look at the board, you compare it with the last page of your notebook, and you write down
, with the date. The notebook grows slowly, and it can answer questions about any day since you started writing. Notice two things: you must look at the board
(a price that changes twice between two visits is only noted once), and you can never fill the notebook for the days

c: On the second run the table exists, so dbt works in three steps. Here is an excerpt of
(we removed blank lines, split long lines and added the three comments):

blocks.text:
-- 1. a temporary table with the changes ('insert' and 'update' rows)
    create temporary table
      "orders_snapshot__dbt_tmp20261021220548660785"
    as (
    with snapshot_query as (
        select * from "practice"."jaffle_shop"."orders"
    ),
    snapshotted_data as (
        select *,
        id as dbt_unique_key
        from "practice"."dbt_adnane"."orders_snapshot"
        where
                dbt_valid_to is null
    ),
    ...
    select * from insertions
    union all
    select * from updates
    );
-- 2. close the old versions
    update "practice"."dbt_adnane"."orders_snapshot"
      as DBT_INTERNAL_TARGET
    set dbt_valid_to = DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_valid_to
    from "orders_snapshot__dbt_tmp20261021220548660785"
      as DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE
    where DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_scd_id::text
          = DBT_INTERNAL_TARGET.dbt_scd_id::text
      and DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_change_type::text
          in ('update'::text, 'delete'::text)
      and DBT_INTERNAL_TARGET.dbt_valid_to is null;
-- 3. insert the new versions and the new keys
    insert into "practice"."dbt_adnane"."orders_snapshot"
      ("id", "user_id", ..., "dbt_scd_id")
    select DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE."id", ...
    from "orders_snapshot__dbt_tmp20261021220548660785"
      as DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE
    where DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_change_type::text = 'insert'::text;
